raw_response:
*Sighs, thinking about the year ahead...*

Aiya, I've been working this land fifty years. My mother-in-law showed me when I first married in. I don't read the papers they put up in the village hall, and those young extension fellows talk too fast. What I know, I know from my own hands and my own eyes. Every year mostly the same, unless the sky tells me different.

We have twelve mu. The eight mu of good land near the road I do wheat then maize, like always. The four mu on the west side — that sandy piece — stays in cotton. Cotton doesn't mind that soil, and we always kept a little cotton for cash. My son and daughter-in-law work in town, so mostly it's me and the old man, and the grandchildren help on weekends and in summer when school lets out.

**Wheat (already in the ground since October):**
Before I sowed last fall I spread the compound — I buy those 50-kg bags at the shop, the 15-15-15 kind, one bag does about one mu. Now in spring when the wheat wakes up, I give it water from the well, and when it starts jointing I topdress with urea — about one bag for every three mu. If I see the leaves yellow early I put more, but I don't like to waste. Spray the yellow-flower weeds once with the medicine the shop sells. I water two, maybe three times — depends on the rain. Pumping that well costs money. Last year I got maybe 400, 420 kg per mu. Neighbor Wang got more but he puts down more fertilizer. His business, my business.

**Maize (goes in right after wheat in June):**
As soon as I cut the wheat, I hire the young man with the rotavator — one day, pay him cash — and we plant maize straight away. Can't wait, the season is short. I buy the hybrid seed at the shop, whatever one the shopkeeper says is good this year, same as my neighbors buy. I put compound down with the seed, then urea when the maize is knee-high. Maybe water it once if the summer rain doesn't come. Spray for the borer worm if I see them. Hope for 450 kg per mu, like most years.

**Cotton (plant late April):**
Cotton is more trouble. I plow that field myself with the small tiller, put down compound, then plant the Bt seed — shop sells it, cost more than other seed but you spray less for the worms. Still I spray maybe four, five times through summer for aphids and bollworm. Water once when it flowers if dry. Then the picking — aiya, my back. My daughter-in-law comes from town on weekends to help, and the grandkids. Three, four pickings from August to October. Maybe 250 kg lint per mu, good year.

Money is always tight. I don't spend what I don't have. If the fertilizer shop raises the price too much I use less, simple.
